# Website React Migration Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax.

**Goal:** Rebuild the OKF4net website as a React app so the chrome (header, nav, footer, docs sidebar) is written once and shared, replacing 13 hand-copied static HTML pages — with **zero visual regression**.

**Architecture:** Vite + React 19 + TypeScript, static-site-generated by `vite-react-ssg` (each route pre-rendered to a real static HTML file for GitHub Pages). The existing design system (`website/assets/site.css`) is reused **verbatim** as global CSS; only structure is componentized. Pages are `.tsx` wrapped in shared `<Layout>` / `<DocsLayout>`. The app lives in `web/`; the current `website/` stays untouched until cutover.

**Tech Stack:** Vite 8, React 19.2, TypeScript, `vite-react-ssg` 0.9.2, `react-router-dom` 6. Node 22 / npm.

## Global Constraints

- New app in `web/` at repo root. Do **not** modify `website/`, `design-system/`, `site-mockups/`, or any `.NET` project — they are out of scope until the cutover step.
- Deploy target: GitHub Pages project site → base path **`/okf4net/`**. Vite `base: '/okf4net/'` **and** react-router `basename: '/okf4net'`.
- **`site.css` is reused verbatim** (copied to `web/src/styles/site.css`, byte-for-byte). No Tailwind, no CSS Modules, no restyling. Componentize structure only.
- Preserve every design-system commitment: `:root` tokens, breakpoints **960px / 720px**, `:focus-visible` ring, `prefers-reduced-motion`, `aria-current` on the active nav link, `aria-pressed` on the home toggle, the inline-SVG `§` favicon, and the three font families (Inter Tight / Inter / Space Mono) at the same weights.
- Output must be **static HTML per route**. A **`.nojekyll`** file must ship at the site root, and a **`404.html`** must exist at the root.
- **Zero visual regression** is the acceptance bar: rendered pages must match the current static site (verified by screenshot diff in the QA task).
- New TS/TSX files: no license header needed (website has none today). Match existing website conventions.

**Reference (current site, to port from):** `website/index.html`, `website/what-okf-is.html`, `website/library.html`, `website/cli.html`, `website/contributing.html`, `website/404.html`, `website/docs/*.html`, `website/assets/site.css`, `website/assets/site.js`. The MCP docs page content is at commit `40fe17f` (`git show 40fe17f:website/docs/mcp.html`). Design rules: `design-system/DESIGN.md`.

### Task 2: Shared chrome + Home page end-to-end

Build the shared `<Layout>` (head/meta, `SiteBar`, `Colophon`) and port the **Home** page — the hardest page (hero + raw⇄rendered toggle) — to validate the whole pattern end-to-end before the bulk port.

**Files:**
- Create: `web/src/components/SiteBar.tsx`, `web/src/components/Colophon.tsx`, `web/src/layouts/Layout.tsx`, `web/src/components/RawRenderedToggle.tsx`
- Modify: `web/src/pages/Home.tsx` (full port), `web/src/routes.tsx`

**Interfaces produced:**
- `Layout({ title, description, children, footerVariant? })` — sets `<title>`/`<meta description>` via `Head`, renders `.topline` + `<SiteBar current=.../>` + `{children}` + `<Colophon variant=.../>`.
- `SiteBar({ current })` where `current` ∈ the site nav keys; uses react-router `NavLink` with `aria-current`.
- `RawRenderedToggle` — `"use client"`-style interactive component porting `website/assets/site.js`.

- [ ] **Step 1: SiteBar** — port `header.bar` from `website/index.html:15-29`. Nav links become react-router `<Link>`/`<NavLink>` (paths: `/`, `/what-okf-is`, `/library`, `/cli`, `/docs`, `/contributing`; the github link stays a plain `<a>`). The active link must render `aria-current="page"` (NavLink does this automatically). Wordmark links to `/`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Colophon** — port `footer.colophon` from `website/index.html:172-182`. Accept a `variant` prop: default renders the `.links` row; `variant="minimal"` (for 404) drops it, matching `website/404.html:56-60`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Layout** — head via vite-react-ssg's head API. Use:
```tsx
import { Head } from 'vite-react-ssg'
```
Render `<Head><title>{title}</title><meta name="description" content={description} /></Head>`, then `<div className="topline" />`, `<SiteBar current={current} />`, children, `<Colophon variant={footerVariant} />`. (If `Head` is not exported by 0.9.2, use the package's documented head mechanism — check its types — and note the adaptation.)

- [ ] **Step 4: RawRenderedToggle** — port the 18-line toggle from `website/assets/site.js` into a React component with `useState` for raw/rendered, toggling the `.visible` class and `aria-pressed`, matching the markup in `website/index.html:39-63`. It must be interactive after hydration.

- [ ] **Step 5: Home page** — port `website/index.html` body (the `.hero` with `RawRenderedToggle`, then the chapters) into `Home.tsx`, wrapped in `<Layout title="OKF4net — knowledge is a directory of markdown files" description="…(copy from website/index.html:7)…" current="home">`. Keep the `.conform` figures verbatim (`218/218 tests · 5 byte-exact golden comparisons`).

### Task 3: Body device components

Extract the ~10 in-body devices as small components that emit the existing `site.css` classes, so ported pages use them instead of raw markup.

**Files:**
- Create: `web/src/components/doc/` — `PageDoc.tsx`, `Chapter.tsx`, `CodeBlock.tsx`, `ConceptGrid.tsx` (+ `Cell`, `Term`), `MapTable.tsx`, `IndexTable.tsx`, `Steps.tsx`, `Warn.tsx`, `Next.tsx`, `Cta.tsx`, `Conform.tsx`, `Tag.tsx`
- Create: `web/src/components/doc/index.ts` (barrel)

**Interfaces produced (used by all page ports):**
- `PageDoc({ path, type, title, lede })` → the `.page-doc` opener (`website/what-okf-is.html:33-44`).
- `Chapter({ id, n?, title, ref, children })` → `section.chapter` + `.chead` (`##` badge + h2 + `.ref`).
- `CodeBlock({ children })` → `pre.block`; callers pass pre-highlighted spans (`<span className="k">…</span>`) as children, matching current markup.
- `ConceptGrid`, `Cell`, `Term`; `MapTable({ head, rows })`; `IndexTable({ rows })`; `Steps({ children })` (`ol.steps`); `Warn({ title, children })`; `Next({ children })` (`p.next`); `Cta({ title, children })`; `Conform({ children })`; `Tag({ children })` (`soon` chip).

- [ ] **Step 2** Add a tiny render check: temporarily mount each in a scratch route or a vitest DOM test asserting the root className (e.g. `Warn` renders `.warn` with a `.t` title). Keep it minimal.

### Task 7: Deploy workflow + 404 + base-path verification

Switch GitHub Pages from uploading `website/` to building `web/` and uploading `web/dist`, and guarantee `404.html` + `.nojekyll` at the root.

**Files:** Modify `.github/workflows/pages.yml`; add a `web/package.json` `postbuild` (or a workflow step) that copies `dist/404/index.html`→`dist/404.html`.

- [ ] **Step 1** Rewrite `pages.yml`: keep triggers on `web/**` + the workflow (and `.github/workflows/pages.yml`); add `actions/setup-node@v4` (node 22, cache npm), `working-directory: web` for `npm ci` and `npm run build`; set `upload-pages-artifact` `path: web/dist`. Keep permissions/concurrency/environment as-is.
- [ ] **Step 2** Ensure `404.html` at root: add `"postbuild": "cp dist/404/index.html dist/404.html"` to `web/package.json` (or a copy step), since GitHub Pages serves `/404.html`. Verify `test -f web/dist/404.html` after build.
- [ ] **Step 3** Base-path verification: serve the built `dist` under the real subpath and confirm no asset 404s:
Run: `cd web && npm run build && npx http-server dist --silent -p 8188` then load `http://localhost:8188/` (assets are requested at `/okf4net/...` → will 404 on a bare root). Correct check: serve so the site sits at `/okf4net/` — e.g. `mkdir -p _serve/okf4net && cp -r dist/* _serve/okf4net/ && npx http-server _serve -p 8188` and load `http://localhost:8188/okf4net/`; confirm assets, favicon, fonts, and an internal nav click all resolve.
- [ ] **Step 4: commit** `git commit -am "ci(web): deploy web/ build to GitHub Pages (setup-node, npm build, 404, base path)"`

## Cutover (after all tasks pass — handled via finishing-a-development-branch, not a build task)

Remove the static `website/` directory (React site is now authoritative), keep `design-system/` + `site-mockups/`, and merge `worktree-website-react` → `main` in a single PR so the deploy switches atomically. The MCP branch `worktree-website-mcp-docs` can then be dropped (its content lives in `web/src/pages/docs/Mcp.tsx`). This step needs explicit user sign-off.

## Self-Review

**Spec coverage:** scaffold+SSG+base path (T1); shared chrome + toggle (T2); body devices (T3); generated sidebar (T4); all 13 pages ported incl. MCP (T2 home, T5 marketing+404, T6 docs) (T5/T6); deploy workflow + 404 + .nojekyll (T1/T7); base-path + parity + a11y + responsive verification (T7/T8); site.css verbatim + no Tailwind (Global Constraints, T1 Step 4). ✅

**Placeholder scan:** The vite-react-ssg API names (`ViteReactSSG`, `RouteRecord`, `Head`) are the one version-sensitive risk; each task that uses them says to adapt to the installed 0.9.2 exports and note it. Page-port tasks specify a precise recipe + source file rather than reproducing all 13 pages' JSX verbatim (mechanical transform of existing, in-repo markup) — deliberate, not a gap.

**Type consistency:** `Layout`/`DocsLayout`/`PageDoc`/`Chapter` prop names are used identically across the port tasks; `docsTree` shape is defined in T4 and consumed by `DocsSidebar`. `current` nav key is threaded from every page through `Layout`→`SiteBar`.
